key_insight: Multi-sensor wearable models predicted perceived exertion better than pulse-rate-only models in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest a potential role for multi-sensor monitoring during ESKD prehabilitation; this study concerns exertion monitoring, not cancer drug discovery.
method: Collected smartwatch pulse rate, electrodermal activity, skin temperature, and accelerometer data during prehabilitation.
Built individualized machine-learning models to predict Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE).
Compared pulse-rate-only regression with multi-feature models in ESKD patients and healthy older controls.
evidence_signal: Among 13 ESKD patients and 13 controls, multi-feature models significantly improved ESKD predictions, achieving an RPE root mean square error of 1.33.
watch_item: The small cohort and individualized modeling require broader validation before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Wearable Sensors Predict Exertion Without Changes in Pulse Rate for Frail End-Stage Kidney Disease Patients
